# docs/ System — Process-Governed Documentation

claude-kit uses a process-governed documentation system. Each documentation
layer is governed by one or more processes defined in `qms/processes/`. The
Process Asset Library (PAL) defines what artifacts exist, where they live,
and how they flow.

For process governance details, see `qms/README.md` and `qms/CATALOG.md`.

## Layer Architecture

```
research/ → requirements/ → architecture/ → specs/ → code → testing/ → benchmarks/
                ↑    ↓                                          ↑
        methodology/ quality/                            operations/ (cross-cutting)
           (meta)   (quality attributes)
                                                      compliance/ (gov overlay)
```

| Layer | Directory | ID Prefix | Governing Process |
|-------|-----------|-----------|-------------------|
| Research | `docs/research/` | — | PROC-LC-001 |
| Requirements | `docs/requirements/` | REQ-XXX | PROC-LC-002 |
| Architecture | `docs/architecture/decisions/` | ADR-XXX | PROC-LC-003 |
| Architecture | `docs/architecture/components/` | — | PROC-LC-003 |
| Specs | `docs/specs/` | SPEC-XXX | PROC-LC-004 |
| Testing | `docs/testing/evidence/` | TEST-XXX | PROC-LC-005 |
| Testing | `docs/testing/regression/` | REG-XXX | PROC-LC-005 |
| Benchmarks | `docs/benchmarks/` | BM-XXX | PROC-ORG-002 |
| Operations | `docs/operations/incidents/` | INC-XXX | PROC-LC-007 |
| Operations | `docs/operations/runbooks/` | RB-XXX | PROC-LC-007 |
| Operations | `docs/operations/migration/` | MIG-XXX | PROC-LC-007 |
| Quality | `docs/quality/` | QA-XXX | PROC-SP-002 |
| Methodology | `docs/methodology/` | — | PROC-ORG-001 |
| Compliance | `docs/compliance/` | — | PROC-GOV-* |

## When to Consult

| You are about to... | Check first |
|---------------------|-------------|
| Start a new feature | `docs/requirements/` for existing REQs, `docs/specs/` for active SPECs |
| Make an architecture decision | `docs/architecture/decisions/` for prior ADRs on the same topic |
| Prepare a release | `docs/specs/` for active SPECs, `docs/testing/` for evidence gaps |
| Debug a production issue | `docs/operations/incidents/` for similar past incidents |
| Change a core subsystem | `docs/architecture/components/` for component documentation |
| Question the requirements basis | `docs/methodology/` for derivation process and evidence grading |
| Evaluate market constraints | `docs/quality/` for compliance, regulatory, and deployment constraints |
| Check regulatory compliance | `docs/compliance/` for control mappings and customer packages |

## When to Update

| You just... | Update |
|-------------|--------|
| Implemented a requirement | Set REQ status to `active`, link to SPEC and ADR |
| Made an architecture decision | Create a new ADR (never edit accepted ADRs) |
| Completed a spec | Set SPEC status to `completed`, create TEST evidence |
| Fixed a regression | Update REG status to `fixed`, note the fix |
| Changed a requirement | Check if downstream ADRs and SPECs need updating |

## Cross-Reference Format

When referencing documents from other layers:

```
See REQ-001 (Domain Knowledge Injection)
```

Always include the document title in parentheses. The validation script
(`scripts/validate-docs.sh`) checks that referenced IDs resolve to real files.

## ADR Immutability Rule

**Never edit an accepted ADR.** To change a decision:

1. Create a new ADR with the next sequential ID
2. Explain in its Context section why the original is being revisited
3. Update the original's status to `superseded-by ADR-YYY` (the **only** allowed edit)

## Creating New Documents

1. Identify the governing process in `qms/CATALOG.md`
2. Check the process's Section 6 (Outputs/Artifacts) for the required template
3. Find the next sequential ID (if `REQ-003` exists, use `REQ-004`)
4. Name the file `<ID>-<short-description>.md` (lowercase, hyphens)
5. Include a `## Traces` section with upstream and downstream links
6. Run `bash scripts/validate-docs.sh` to verify compliance

## Validation

Docs structure is validated by `scripts/validate-docs.sh` (Layer 4) and process
framework is validated by `qms/scripts/validate-processes.sh` (Layer 5) as part
of the `fast-validate` CI job.
